messages.content:
Let

\[ S = \sum_{k=0}^{2026} k \binom{2k}{k} 2^k. \]

Compute the remainder when \( S \) is divided by 2027. (Note that 2027 is prime.)

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(p=2027\) and \(m=(p-1)/2=1013\). We work modulo \(p\).

For \(0\le k\le m\),
\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv (-4)^k\binom{m}{k}\pmod p,
\]
since
\[
(-4)^k\binom{m}{k}
=\prod_{j=1}^k \frac{-4\left(\frac{p+1}{2}-j\right)}{j}
\equiv \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{2(2j-1)}{j}
=\binom{2k}{k}.
\]
For \(m<k\le p-1\), the prime \(p\) divides \((2k)!\) but not \(k!\), so \(\binom{2k}{k}\equiv 0\pmod p\).

Thus
\[
S\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{m} k(-4)^k\binom{m}{k}2^k
=\sum_{k=0}^{m} k\binom{m}{k}(-8)^k.
\]
Using \(\sum k\binom{m}{k}x^k = mx(1+x)^{m-1}\),
\[
S\equiv m(-8)(1-8)^{m-1}
=-8m(-7)^{1012}.
\]
Since \(8m=4p-4\equiv -4\pmod p\), we get
\[
S\equiv 4(-7)^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Now compute \((-7)^{1012}\). By quadratic reciprocity,
\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)=-\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)
=-\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)=-1,
\]
so \(7^{1013}\equiv -1\pmod{2027}\). Hence
\[
7^{1012}\equiv -7^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]
Since \(7\cdot 1448\equiv 1\pmod{2027}\), we have
\[
7^{1012}\equiv -1448\equiv 579\pmod{2027}.
\]
Therefore
\[
S\equiv 4\cdot 579=2316\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
